record.original_question: Is the Caratheodory metric complete on a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.3.1 Is c complete on a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded pseudoconvex domain with smooth boundary. For points $p, q \in \Omega$, define the Carathéodory pseudodistance by
$$ c_\Omega(p,q) = \sup\bigl\{ \rho(f(p), f(q)) : f : \Omega \to \mathbb{D} \text{ holomorphic} \bigr\}, $$
where $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ is the unit disc and $\rho$ denotes the Poincaré distance on $\mathbb{D}$. The domain $\Omega$ is said to be Carathéodory complete if $(\Omega, c_\Omega)$ is a complete metric space (equivalently, every $c_\Omega$-Cauchy sequence converges to a point of $\Omega$).

Question: Is every bounded pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth boundary Carathéodory complete?
artifact.category_tag: Invariant metrics in several complex variables
artifact.status_search_result: The question of Carathéodory completeness for bounded smooth pseudoconvex domains remains open in general. Completeness is known for strongly pseudoconvex domains, for bounded complete Reinhardt pseudoconvex domains, and for finite-type domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$ and certain corank-one situations. Sibony-type counterexamples to Carathéodory completeness exist among bounded pseudoconvex domains without smooth boundary, but the smooth-boundary case appears unresolved in the recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Pseudoconvexity, Analytic Discs, and Invariant Metrics (Krantz)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of boundary behavior of the Carathéodory and Kobayashi metrics on strongly pseudoconvex domains and special weakly pseudoconvex domains.
status_evidence.claim: Carathéodory completeness is established on strongly pseudoconvex bounded smooth domains, but general weakly pseudoconvex smooth domains are not covered.

status_evidence.title: About the Caratheodory Completeness of all Reinhardt Domains
status_evidence.snippet: Any bounded complete Reinhardt pseudoconvex domain is complete in the sense of the Carathéodory distance.
status_evidence.claim: Carathéodory completeness is known for special classes such as bounded complete Reinhardt pseudoconvex domains.

status_evidence.title: Estimation of the Carathéodory distance on pseudoconvex domains of finite type
status_evidence.snippet: Estimates of Carathéodory distance for finite-type pseudoconvex domains with Levi form of corank at most one.
status_evidence.claim: Progress toward Carathéodory completeness on smooth pseudoconvex domains is restricted to finite-type / corank-one cases.
